en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 4 deals, the strategies behind them · 9 November 2026

🔹 Valsoft Corporation (via TAG Software Group) (acquisition and long-term development of vertical market software, Canada) acquires Chalco (content and product information lifecycle management software platform for luxury brands and distribution, Italy and Switzerland).
Chalco, developed within Hyphen-Group for over twenty-five years, is acquired via a new structure, Chalco Technologies Srl.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Valsoft gains intellectual property and international expansion capability, while the seller retains its local goodwill — a surgical separation between technological assets and commercial network.

🔹 Huisman (design and manufacturing of heavy equipment for offshore and energy, Netherlands) acquires Future Production (modular solutions for maintenance, modification, and operation of offshore platforms and renewable energy, Kristiansand, Norway).
Future Production, with around forty employees, has completed over 650 deliveries on more than 90 platforms since 1999. Its model relies on in-house engineering and outsourced manufacturing.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Huisman is not buying physical assets but rare engineering expertise and a network of contacts in recovering markets — precisely what cannot be quickly rebuilt in an upturn.

🔹 Amplifon (hearing aid distribution and fitting, Italy) acquires GN's hearing division (manufacturing and marketing of hearing aids, a Danish group active in audio and communications).
The European Commission's authorization complements approvals already obtained in Australia and the United States. Closing is expected before year-end, with operational integration preparations underway.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Simultaneously obtaining European, American, and Australian approvals indicates that competition authorities did not deem the merger likely to close off the audiology market.

🔹 Michiels Foods (food, family business based in Zulte, East Flanders) acquires Billiebubs (breakfast products and snacks for babies and young children, Kortrijk).
The acquisition aims to expand Michiels Foods' activities into the consumer market, entering a segment with high perceived value and stringent regulatory requirements.

fr.text:
M&A : les 4 annonces récentes de l'édito du 9 novembre 2026.

🔹 Valsoft Corporation (via TAG Software Group) (𝑎𝑐𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑠𝑖𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑎̀ 𝑙𝑜𝑛𝑔 𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑠 𝑎̀ 𝑣𝑜𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑠𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑜𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒, 𝐶𝑎𝑛𝑎𝑑𝑎) rachète Chalco (𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑢 𝑐𝑦𝑐𝑙𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑣𝑖𝑒 𝑑𝑢 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑛𝑢 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑙'𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑡 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑢𝑥𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑏𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛, 𝐼𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑆𝑢𝑖𝑠𝑠𝑒).
Chalco, développée au sein de Hyphen-Group depuis plus de vingt-cinq ans, est reprise via une nouvelle structure, Chalco Technologies Srl.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Valsoft récupère la propriété intellectuelle et la capacité d'expansion internationale, tandis que le vendeur conserve son fonds de commerce local — une séparation chirurgicale entre actif technologique et réseau commercial.

🔹 Huisman (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑓𝑎𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑'𝑒́𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠 𝑙𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑑𝑠) rachète Future Production (𝑠𝑜𝑙𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑙𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙𝑎 𝑚𝑎𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒).
Future Production, une quarantaine de personnes, a réalisé plus de 650 livraisons sur plus de 90 plateformes depuis 1999. Son modèle repose sur une ingénierie internalisée et une fabrication sous-traitée.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Huisman n'achète pas des actifs physiques mais une expertise d'ingénierie rare et un carnet de contacts sur des marchés en reprise — précisément ce qui ne se reconstruit pas vite dans un cycle haussier.

🔹 Amplifon (𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑏𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑎𝑝𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑒𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑎𝑔𝑒 𝑎𝑢𝑑𝑖𝑡𝑖𝑓, 𝐼𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑒) rachète la branche hearing de GN (𝑓𝑎𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑚𝑒𝑟𝑐𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑'𝑎𝑝𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑒𝑖𝑙𝑠 𝑎𝑢𝑑𝑖𝑡𝑖𝑓𝑠).
L'autorisation de la Commission européenne complète les feux verts déjà obtenus en Australie et aux États-Unis. Le closing est attendu avant la fin de l'année, la préparation de l'intégration opérationnelle étant en cours.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Obtenir simultanément les feux verts européen, américain et australien signale que les autorités de concurrence n'ont pas jugé le rapprochement de nature à fermer le marché de l'audiologie.

🔹 Michiels Foods (𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛, 𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑠𝑒 𝑓𝑎𝑚𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑒 𝑏𝑎𝑠𝑒́𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝑍𝑢𝑙𝑡𝑒, 𝐹𝑙𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑟𝑒 𝑜𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑒) rachète Billiebubs (𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑡𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑒𝑡𝑖𝑡-𝑑𝑒́𝑗𝑒𝑢𝑛𝑒𝑟 𝑒𝑡 𝑠𝑛𝑎𝑐𝑘𝑠 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑏𝑒́𝑏𝑒́𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑗𝑒𝑢𝑛𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑛𝑓𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑠).
L'acquisition vise à élargir les activités de Michiels Foods vers le marché grand public, en entrant sur un segment à forte valeur perçue et à exigences réglementaires élevées.

🔹 Granit (automation of administrative management for practices, clinics, and healthcare facilities, using artificial intelligence) — €5m · Seed.
Founded in March 2026, Granit claims 250 equipped facilities in less than eight months of existence, in a market known for slow adoption and demanding compliance.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Convincing 250 healthcare facilities in less than a year is a sign of real traction, but the true test will be retention if integration with existing business software proves imperfect.
